events.title: Coastal Flood Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding. For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6- 8 feet, sets up to 10-12 feet along west-facing beaches. * WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 AM PST this morning. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 4 AM this morning to 1 PM PST Friday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 1 PM Wednesday to 4 AM PST Friday. Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the time of the morning high tide, with peak tides trending from 7 AM today to 10 AM on Friday. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides peak through Wednesday at 7.9- 8.3 feet, likely breaking the all-time tidal records set back in late October. Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 2-5 feet through Wednesday morning, but a long period west swell arrives Wednesday afternoon, bringing a sharp increase to the surf for late Wednesday into Thursday. Breaking waves may reach 6-8 feet with local sets up to 10 feet on west- facing beaches. Surf lowers to 5-7 feet by Friday morning's high tide.

events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Up to 2 to 4 feet of inundation above ground level possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Areas along the beaches, Pamlico Sound, and adjacent tidal creeks, and Ocracoke Island. * WHEN...From Wednesday evening through Friday morning. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. This includes impacts to Hwy 12. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure may be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King Tides will be peaking on Wednesday and Thursday before gradually lowering which will continue to bring elevated water levels to the area through much of the week. The King Tides will be exacerbated by a strong coastal low impacting the area Wednesday evening into Thursday morning. The higher of the high tide cycles will be during the morning hours each day this week. Initially ocean overwash will be a concern as 10-15 ft seas impact the area beaches. This will be of greatest concern across the more vulnerable dunes along Hwy 12. However as winds switch to a SW direction Thursday afternoon and evening minor water level rises (around 1-2 ft) on soundside locations of Hatteras and Ocracoke Island will be possible as water sloshes back towards the eastern end of the Pamlico Sound.

events.description: * WHAT...One to two feet of inundation above ground level possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Ocean and Coastal Ocean. * WHEN...From Thursday morning through Friday afternoon. * IMPACTS...At this level, widespread roadway flooding occurs in coastal and bayside communities and along inland tidal waterways. and property. Follow the recommendations of local emergency

events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be possible. * WHERE...A portion of northwest Washington, including the following county, Mason. * WHEN...From Wednesday morning through Sunday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - A series of storms will bring roughly 3 to 6 inches of rainfall to the southern slopes of the Olympics through Thursday with snow levels rising to around 5000 to 5500 feet on Tuesday, and as high as 6000 to 6500 feet on Wednesday. The combination of heavy rain and relatively high snow levels is expected to push the Skokomish River near Potlach above flood stage by midweek. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...1 1/2 to 2 1/2 feet of inundation above ground level possible in vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline. * WHERE...In Connecticut, Southern New Haven County. In New York, Bronx, Northwest Suffolk, Northern Queens and Northern Nassau Counties. * WHEN...From Thursday morning through Friday afternoon high tides. * COASTAL FLOOD IMPACTS...Widespread moderate flooding of vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline, including roads, parking lots, parks, lawns, and homes and businesses with basements near the waterfront. Numerous road closures are likely, and vehicles parked in vulnerable areas near the waterfront will likely become flooded. Flooding will also extend inland from the waterfront along tidal rivers and bays. * SHORELINE IMPACTS...Breaking waves of 3 to 6 ft will result in areas of dune erosion and localized overwashes. Wave splashover will exacerbate flooding of roadways and vulnerable structures behind protective dunes and seawalls. There is potential for isolated damage to shoreline and marina structures as well. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The highest water levels are likely with the Thursday morning and evening high tides, potentially extending into the Friday afternoon high tides. The forecast has been leaned towards a higher end water level scenario to provide a bit of safety margin. If the timing of strongest winds is quicker than currently forecast the peak water level forecast could be increased by a few tenths for Thursday morning. if slower the Thursday morning forecast could be lowered slightly.

location.region: Southern New Haven; Bronx; Northwest Suffolk; Northern Queens; Northern Nassau

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 24 at 4:57PM EST until November 27 at 3:00PM EST by NWS Upton NY
weather.description:
* WHAT...1 1/2 to 2 1/2 feet of inundation above ground level
possible in vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline.

* WHERE...In Connecticut, Southern New Haven County. In New
York, Bronx, Northwest Suffolk, Northern Queens and Northern
Nassau Counties.

* WHEN...From Thursday morning through Friday afternoon high
tides.

* COASTAL FLOOD IMPACTS...Widespread moderate flooding of
vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline, including
roads, parking lots, parks, lawns, and homes and businesses
with basements near the waterfront. Numerous road closures are
likely, and vehicles parked in vulnerable areas near the
waterfront will likely become flooded. Flooding will also
extend inland from the waterfront along tidal rivers and bays.

* SHORELINE IMPACTS...Breaking waves of 3 to 6 ft will result in
areas of dune erosion and localized overwashes. Wave
splashover will exacerbate flooding of roadways and vulnerable
structures behind protective dunes and seawalls. There is
potential for isolated damage to shoreline and marina
structures as well.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The highest water levels are likely with
the Thursday morning and evening high tides, potentially
extending into the Friday afternoon high tides. The forecast has
been leaned towards a higher end water level scenario to provide
a bit of safety margin. If the timing of strongest winds is
quicker than currently forecast the peak water level forecast
could be increased by a few tenths for Thursday morning. if
slower the Thursday morning forecast could be lowered slightly.
weather.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Warning means that moderate or major tidal
flooding is occurring or imminent. Be prepared for rising water
levels and take appropriate action to protect life and property.
Follow the recommendations of local emergency management
officials.

Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The water may be
deeper than you think it is. You will be putting yourself in
danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to costly
repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that minor tidal flooding is
expected. Minor tidal flooding often results in some road
closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

events.title: Coastal Flood Warning
events.description: * WHAT...Significant coastal flooding expected. * WHERE...Orange County Coastal Areas. * WHEN...Through 1 PM PST Friday. Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the time of the morning high tide, with peak tides trending from 8 AM today to 10 AM on Friday. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides peak each day through Thursday at 7.9-8.3 feet, likely breaking the all-time tidal records set back in late October. A long period west swell arrives late this afternoon and will bring elevated to high surf by Thursday morning's high tide. Breaking waves may reach 4-6 feet with local sets up to 7-8 feet on west-facing beaches. Surf lowers to 3-5 feet by Friday morning's high tide.

events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1 foot of inundation above ground level expected in vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline. For the Coastal Flood Warning, 2 to 3, locally 3 1/2 ft of inundation above ground level expected in vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline. For the Coastal Flood Watch, up to 2 to 3 ft of inundation above ground level possible in vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline. * WHERE...Southern Nassau County. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 11 AM EST this morning. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 7 AM Thursday to 6 AM EST Friday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Friday morning through Friday afternoon. * COASTAL FLOOD IMPACTS...Widespread moderate to locally major flooding of vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline, including roads, parking lots, parks, lawns, and homes and businesses with basements near the waterfront. Numerous road closures are likely, and vehicles parked in vulnerable areas near the waterfront will likely become flooded. Flooding will also extend inland from the waterfront along tidal rivers and bays. * SHORELINE IMPACTS...Breaking waves of 8 to 12 ft will result in widespread beach flooding and dune erosion widespread beach flooding and dune erosion during times of high tide. There is potential for localized overwashes resulting in some flooding of roadways and vulnerable structures behind protective dunes. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The highest water levels are likely with the Thursday morning and evening high tides, potentially extending into the Friday morning high tides. This forecast will be refined over the next 12 to 24 hours as timing of wind forcing with respect to Thursday AM/PM high tides becomes more clear. The forecast has been leaned towards a higher end water level scenario to provide a bit of safety margin. If the timing of strongest winds is quicker than currently forecast the peak water level forecast could be increased by a few tenths for Thursday morning. if slower the Thursday morning forecast could be lowered slightly.

events.title: Flood Warning
events.description: ...The National Weather Service in Seattle has issued a Flood Warning for the following rivers in Washington... Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County. .Heavy rain over the Olypics overnight plus an additional 2-4 inches of rain, with snow levels well above mountain tops will drive the Skokomish River above flood stage this afternoon to above Moderate flood. * WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast. This approaches the flood of record. * WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch. * WHEN...From this afternoon to Friday evening. * IMPACTS...At 17.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause moderate flooding, with deep and quick flood waters inundating some residential areas, many roads, and much of the farm land in the Skokomish Valley. Inundated roads include the Skokomish Valley road, Bourgault Road West, Purdy Cutoff Road, and Highway 106. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 8:30 AM PST Wednesday the stage was 15.6 feet. - Forecast...The river will rise above flood stage this afternoon to 17.9 feet late tonight. It will then fall below flood stage late Friday morning. Further rises through the weekend are likely, with exceeding flood stage possible. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

location.region: Mason, WA

weather.headline: Flood Warning issued November 25 at 9:30AM PST until November 27 at 7:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
weather.description:
...The National Weather Service in Seattle has issued a Flood Warning
for the following rivers in Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

.Heavy rain over the Olypics overnight plus an additional 2-4 inches
of rain, with snow levels well above mountain tops will drive the
Skokomish River above flood stage this afternoon to above Moderate
flood.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast. This approaches the flood of
record.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...From this afternoon to Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 17.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause moderate
flooding, with deep and quick flood waters inundating some
residential areas, many roads, and much of the farm land in the
Skokomish Valley. Inundated roads include the Skokomish Valley
road, Bourgault Road West, Purdy Cutoff Road, and Highway 106.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM PST Wednesday the stage was 15.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise above flood stage this afternoon
to 17.9 feet late tonight. It will then fall below flood stage
late Friday morning. Further rises through the weekend are
likely, with exceeding flood stage possible.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this afternoon at 530 PM PST.
weather.areaDesc: Mason, WA

events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 8 to 12 feet expected in the surf zone. For the Coastal Flood Warning, 2 to 4 feet of inundation above ground level expected in low- lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Northern Outer Banks. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 10 AM EST Friday. closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The

yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Up to one foot of inundation above ground level expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways (3.1 to 12.9 feet Mean Lower Low Water). * WHERE...Eastern Essex MA, Southeast Middlesex MA, Suffolk MA, Eastern Norfolk MA, Eastern Plymouth MA, Barnstable MA, Dukes MA and Nantucket MA Counties. * WHEN...From 8 AM to 3 PM EST Friday. * IMPACTS...Shallow pockets of flooding less than one foot deep affects the lowest lying areas along the coast, including Morrissey Boulevard in Boston. Most roads remain passable. Flooding up to one foot deep affects coastal roads on the North Shore from Salem to Gloucester and Newburyport. Rough surf will cause flooding on some coastal roads around the time of high tide due to splashover. Roads remain passable. Low lying areas and roads near Nantucket Harbor, including Easy Street, may experience pockets of shallow flooding less than one foot deep.

location.region: Eastern Essex; Southeast Middlesex; Suffolk; Eastern Norfolk; Eastern Plymouth; Barnstable; Dukes; Nantucket

For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 8 AM to 4 PM EST Friday. * COASTAL FLOOD IMPACTS...Widespread moderate flooding of vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline, including roads, parking lots, parks, lawns, and homes and businesses with basements near the waterfront. Numerous road closures are likely, and vehicles parked in vulnerable areas near the waterfront will likely become flooded. Flooding will also extend inland from the waterfront along tidal rivers and bays. * SHORELINE IMPACTS...Breaking waves of 4 to 8 ft will result in areas of dune erosion and localized overwashes. Wave splashover will exacerbate flooding of roadways and vulnerable structures behind protective dunes and seawalls. There is potential for isolated damage to shoreline and marina structures as well. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The highest water levels are likely with the Thursday morning and evening high tides. The forecast has been leaned towards a higher end water level scenario to provide a bit of safety margin. If the timing of strongest winds is quicker than currently forecast the peak water level forecast could be increased by a few tenths for Thursday morning, and if slower the Thursday morning forecast could be lowered slightly. Similarly if strongest winds linger later into the evening, the Thursday evening water level forecast could be a few tenths higher.

For the High Surf Advisory, from noon Thursday to 9 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Damaging flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beaches (especially from Faria Beach to Silver Strand Beach), roads, and structures. events.title: Flood Warning
events.description: ...Forecast flooding changed from Moderate to Major severity for the following rivers in Washington... Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County. .Heavy rain over the Olympics overnight with snow levels well above mountain tops has driven the Skokomish River to major flood stage this morning. * WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast. This approaches the flood of record. * WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch. * WHEN...Until Friday morning. * IMPACTS...At 18.0 feet, the Skokomish River will cause major, near record flooding throughout the Skokomish Valley. Deep and swift flood waters will inundate residential areas, many roads including SR 106, and much of the farm land. Flooding will occur all along the river including headwaters, tributaries, and other streams within and near the Skokomish River Basin. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 3:30 AM PST Thursday the stage was 17.97 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 3:30 AM PST Thursday was 17.97 feet. - Forecast...The river will rise to 18.1 feet late this morning. It will then fall below flood stage on Friday morning. Further rises through the weekend are likely, with exceeding flood stage possible. - Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.8 feet on 03/19/1997. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

location.region: Mason, WA

SR 106, and much of the farm land.   Flooding will occur all along
the river including headwaters, tributaries, and other streams
within and near the Skokomish River Basin.

at 3:30 AM PST Thursday was 17.97 feet.

higher ground.

weather.description:

expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Ocean and Coastal Ocean.

* WHEN...From 6 AM this morning to 3 PM EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...At this level, widespread roadway flooding occurs in
coastal and bayside communities and along inland tidal
waterways. Many roads become impassable. Some damage to
vulnerable structures may begin to occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The most severe and impactful high tide
will be with Thursday morning's high tide, when major tidal
flooding is forecast. Additional minor to moderate tidal
flooding is forecast with Thursday night's high tide.

weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Warning means that moderate or major tidal
flooding is occurring or imminent. Be prepared for rising water
levels and take appropriate action to protect life and property.
Follow the recommendations of local emergency management
officials.

Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The water may be
deeper than you think it is. You will be putting yourself in
danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to costly
repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 830 PM PST.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Up to one foot of inundation above ground level expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Kent MD. * WHEN...From 6 PM this evening to midnight EST Friday night. * IMPACTS...At this level, flooding begins on the most vulnerable roads in bayside communities and along tidal waterways. Some partial or full road closures are possible. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Tide levels could reach near moderate flood stage during this evening's high tide.

location.region: Kent

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 26 at 2:09PM EST until November 28 at 12:00AM EST by NWS Mount Holly NJ
weather.description:
* WHAT...Up to one foot of inundation above ground level
expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Kent MD.

* WHEN...From 6 PM this evening to midnight EST Friday night.

* IMPACTS...At this level, flooding begins on the most
vulnerable roads in bayside communities and along tidal
waterways. Some partial or full road closures are possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Tide levels could reach near moderate flood
stage during this evening's high tide.
weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that minor tidal flooding is
expected. Minor tidal flooding often results in some road
closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.
weather.areaDesc: Kent

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Neuse River near Clayton.

The next statement will be issued Friday morning at 1000 AM EST.

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 26 at 7:55PM EST until November 27 at 3:00PM EST by NWS Mount Holly NJ
weather.description:
* WHAT...Up to one foot of inundation above ground level in low-
lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Inland Sussex and Delaware Beaches.

* WHEN...Until 3 PM EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...At this level, flooding begins on the most vulnerable
roads in coastal and bayside communities, and along inland tidal
waterways. Some partial or full road closures are possible.
weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Warning means that moderate or major tidal
flooding is occurring or imminent. Be prepared for rising water
levels and take appropriate action to protect life and property.
Follow the recommendations of local emergency management
officials.

Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The water may be
deeper than you think it is. You will be putting yourself in
danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to costly
repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Statement, isolated minor coastal
flooding. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents.

afternoon.

shore and call or wave for help.

weather.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast to continue. This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...Until Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 17.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause moderate
flooding, with deep and quick flood waters inundating some
residential areas, many roads, and much of the farm land in the
Skokomish Valley. Inundated roads include the Skokomish Valley
road, Bourgault Road West, Purdy Cutoff Road, and Highway 106.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:30 PM PST Thursday the stage was 17.9 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 2:30 PM PST Thursday was 17.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to continue to hover near a
crest of 17.9 feet through this evening. It will then fall below
flood stage tomorrow morning.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at midnight PST.

events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by an upstream dam release is expected. * WHERE...Central Yuma County in southwestern Arizona... * WHEN...Until 300 PM MST Monday. * IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 202 PM MST, a streamflow gauge near Dateland continues to steadily rise and is now showing a depth of just above 7.5 feet with flow around 1250 cfs. This gauge is forecasted to reach action stage (8 ft) on Friday. Flooding is expected along the Gila River within the warned area. - Some locations that will experience flooding include... Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.description: Rain will mix with or changeover to wet snow as temperatures quickly drop into the lower to mid 30s this evening. If traveling over higher elevations, especially overnight, you should expect poor visibility with periods of wet snow and slushy road surfaces. Snow and rain will diminish in intensity Friday before gradually ending.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Up to one foot of inundation above ground level expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways (3.1 to 12.9 feet Mean Lower Low Water). * WHERE...Eastern Essex MA, Southeast Middlesex MA, Suffolk MA, Eastern Norfolk MA, Eastern Plymouth MA, Barnstable MA, Dukes MA and Nantucket MA Counties. * WHEN...From 8 AM to 3 PM EST Friday. * IMPACTS...Shallow pockets of flooding less than one foot deep affects the lowest lying areas along the coast, including Morrissey Boulevard in Boston. Most roads remain passable. Flooding up to one foot deep affects coastal roads on the North Shore from Salem to Gloucester and Newburyport. Rough surf will cause flooding on some coastal roads around the time of high tide due to splashover. Roads remain passable. Low lying areas and roads near Nantucket Harbor, including Easy Street, may experience pockets of shallow flooding less than one foot deep.

events.title: Special Weather Statement
events.description: Light rain transitioning to light snow has begun in areas across north Georgia this evening as expected. Temperatures below approximately 2500' remain just at or above freezing, meaning no significant accumulations are expected but snow could briefly linger on elevated or grassy surfaces through the night. Above 2500' temperatures have fallen to at or below freezing. Up to an inch of accumulation could occur in these locations with isolated amounts of around 2" along some of the higher peaks. Overall travel impacts should be minimal. Recent warm temperatures should keep roadways mostly clear, though care should be had on bridges and overpasses, especially in elevated locations. For more information or to report snowfall amounts at your location, please visit www.weather.gov/atlanta.

weather.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

through flooded areas.

dangers of flooding.

events.title: Winter Weather Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Snow and blowing snow expected. Total snow accumulations 3 to 6 inches. Winds gusting as high as 40 to 50 mph. Visibilities reduced to one half mile or less due to blowing snow. * WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island. * WHEN...Until 6 PM AKST Friday. * IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Areas of blowing snow could significantly reduce visibility. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest chances of blowing snow are on Nunivak Island and along the Kuskokwim Delta Coast north of Kipnuk. Southeast winds become westerly early Friday morning. The strongest wind gusts are expected Friday morning after winds become westerly. Conditions are expected to gradually improve late Friday afternoon as snowfall tapers off and winds begin to decrease.

events.title: Flood Warning
events.description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Above Lake Harney affecting Seminole County. .Rainfall working through the basin has caused river levels on the St. Johns Above Lake Harney near Geneva to remain within Major Flood Stage, above its previous record flood stage. River levels are forecast to hold near a crest of 13.2 feet through late week, before beginning a very slow decline within Major flood stage this weekend and early next week. For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Major flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast. The river crest has surpassed its previous flood of record. * WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney. * WHEN...Until further notice. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 7:30 AM EST Friday the stage was 13.2 feet. - Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 7:30 AM EST Friday was 13.2 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to remain within Major Flood Stage, steady at 13.2 feet through tonight. A slow decline may begin over the weekend into early next week. - Flood stage is 8.0 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

weather.description:
* WHAT...Coastal Flooding with water levels 1.5 to 3.0 feet
above the highest tide line possible.

* WHERE...Kipnuk, Kongiganak, and Kwigillingok.

* WHEN...UNTIL 6 AM Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Potential flooding of low lying areas, including
lowest portions of boardwalks. Coastal erosion possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A long duration of onshore winds combined
with higher-than-normal tides will increase the potential for
elevated water levels, high surf, and coastal erosion Friday
night. Tides will remain higher than normal into the middle of
next week.
weather.instruction:
A coastal flood advisory indicates that onshore winds and tides
will combine to generate flooding of low areas along the shore.

events.title: High Surf Warning
events.description: ...HIGH SURF WARNING IN EFFECT FOR NORTH AND WEST FACING SHORES OF NIIHAU KAUAI OAHU MOLOKAI...AND NORTH FACING SHORES OF MAUI AND THE BIG ISLAND... .An extra-large north-northwest (330 to 350 degree) swell will maintain warning level surf this morning and subside through the day to advisory levels by this evening. * WHAT...For north-facing shores, surf heights 20 to 30 ft this morning, subsiding to 20 to 25 ft this afternoon. For west- facing shores, surf 12 to 16 ft this morning, subsiding to 10 to 14 ft this afternoon. * WHERE...North and west-facing shores of Niihau, Kauai, Oahu, Molokai, and north facing shores of Maui and the Big Island. * WHEN...Until 6 PM HST this evening. * IMPACTS...High. Expect very strong breaking waves and powerful currents. Waves breaking in channel entrances may make navigating the channels dangerous.

weather.description:
...HIGH SURF WARNING IN EFFECT FOR NORTH AND WEST FACING SHORES
OF NIIHAU KAUAI OAHU MOLOKAI...AND NORTH FACING SHORES OF MAUI
AND THE BIG ISLAND...

.An extra-large north-northwest (330 to 350 degree) swell will
maintain warning level surf this morning and subside through the
day to advisory levels by this evening.

* WHAT...For north-facing shores, surf heights 20 to 30 ft this
morning, subsiding to 20 to 25 ft this afternoon. For west-
facing shores, surf 12 to 16 ft this morning, subsiding to 10 to
14 ft this afternoon.

* WHERE...North and west-facing shores of Niihau, Kauai, Oahu,
Molokai, and north facing shores of Maui and the Big Island.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM HST this evening.

* IMPACTS...High. Expect very strong breaking waves and powerful
currents. Waves breaking in channel entrances may make
navigating the channels dangerous.
weather.instruction:
Stay away from the shoreline along the affected coasts. Be
prepared for road closures. Postpone entering or leaving channels
affected by the high surf until the surf subsides.

events.title: Flood Warning
events.description: ...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Washington... Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County. * WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast. This approaches the flood of record. * WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch. * WHEN...Until late tonight. * IMPACTS...At 17.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause moderate flooding, with deep and quick flood waters inundating some residential areas, many roads, and much of the farm land in the Skokomish Valley. Inundated roads include the Skokomish Valley road, Bourgault Road West, Purdy Cutoff Road, and Highway 106. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 4:30 AM PST Friday the stage was 17.6 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 4:30 AM PST Friday was 17.9 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to continue to gradually recede and fall into minor flood stage later this morning. It will then fall below flood stage this evening. - Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.6 feet on 10/20/2003. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

location.region: Mason, WA

weather.headline: Flood Warning issued November 27 at 5:23AM PST until November 28 at 1:00AM PST by NWS Seattle WA
weather.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and minor flooding is
forecast. This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...Until late tonight.

* IMPACTS...At 17.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause moderate
flooding, with deep and quick flood waters inundating some
residential areas, many roads, and much of the farm land in the
Skokomish Valley. Inundated roads include the Skokomish Valley
road, Bourgault Road West, Purdy Cutoff Road, and Highway 106.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 4:30 AM PST Friday the stage was 17.6 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 4:30 AM PST Friday was 17.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to continue to gradually recede
and fall into minor flood stage later this morning. It will then
fall below flood stage this evening.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.6
feet on 10/20/2003.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this afternoon at 130 PM PST.
weather.areaDesc: Mason, WA

events.title: Special Weather Statement
events.description: Areas of rain and snow will continue through mid morning, before tapering off this afternoon. Most areas will see the rain, but locally heavier bands will change the rain to snow. Where these bands of snow fall, a quick accumulation of up to an inch will be possible, mainly on grassy areas. Roads could develop a slush and become slick temporarily, along with a quick reduction in visibility. If drivers encounter these heavier bands of snow, slow down by laying off the gas pedal, and leave extra room between your vehicle and others.

events.description: Rain will mix with or change to snow early this morning. Temperatures will be marginal for snow accumulation, and with the ground being warm, it will further limit the potential. events.title: Special Weather Statement
events.description: Light snow showers are expected across the mountains near the Tennessee border and across Macon and northern Jackson counties overnight. By this morning, snowfall of 1 to 2 inches, with locally higher amounts is possible across the higher elevations of western Graham and western Macon Counties, as well as the higher elevations of the Smokies. A dusting to up to an inch is possible across the upslope areas of the Northern Mountains. The snow may briefly mix with light freezing rain or drizzle before ending this morning. While a brief period of wintry weather is possible in the valleys across the Tennessee border counties this morning, little-to-no accumulation is expected in these areas. Motorists planning travel across the high elevations of southwest North Carolina this morning should plan for potential slick spots on roads.

location.region: Avery; Madison; Yancey; Mitchell; Swain; Haywood; Graham; Northern Jackson; Macon

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.7 ft of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 13 to 19 ft. * WHERE...The Pacific Coast. * WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Saturday morning. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide is expected to be 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at 12:31 PM Friday, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:28 PM Saturday, and 0.9 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) at 2:32 PM Sunday. These predictions include up to 1.3 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.7 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Saturday
morning. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST
Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high
tide is expected to be 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at
12:31 PM Friday, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:28 PM
Saturday, and 0.9 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) at 2:32 PM
Sunday. These predictions include up to 1.3 ft of surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High
tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
weather.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

events.title: Special Weather Statement
events.description: Areas of light snow will continue across portions of far North Georgia through around mid-morning. At elevations below 2500 feet, little to no accumulation is expected, though a dusting may occur on grassy and elevated surfaces. At elevations near or above 2500 feet, total accumulations up to 2 inches are possible. Overall, travel impacts should be minimal, as recent warm temperatures should keep most roadways clear. However, motorists should exercise caution, particularly on bridges and overpasses and along roadways at higher elevations where isolated slick spots may develop. For more information or to report snowfall amounts at your location, please visit www.weather.gov/atlanta.

weather.description:
* WHAT...One to two feet of inundation above ground level in low-

* WHERE...Kent MD.

* WHEN...Until midnight EST tonight.

* IMPACTS...At this level, widespread roadway flooding occurs in
bayside communities and along tidal waterways. Some roads
become impassable. Minor damage to vulnerable structures may
begin to occur.
weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Warning means that moderate or major tidal
flooding is occurring or imminent. Be prepared for rising water
levels and take appropriate action to protect life and property.
Follow the recommendations of local emergency management
officials.

Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The water may be
deeper than you think it is. You will be putting yourself in
danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to costly
repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

events.title: Special Weather Statement
events.description: We will continue to some light rain or snow in the lower elevations with little or no snow accumulation overnight, but the higher elevations especially above 2500 feet will be primarily snow overnight into Friday morning. While the ground is warm, some of the higher terrain of the Plateau, southwest Virginia, the east Tennessee mountains, and the mountains of southwest North Carolina will see around an inch of snow accumulation. A few mountain peaks may see accumulations in the 2 to 3 inch range. While the ground is still fairly warm this early in the season, be alert for slippery spots on roadways if traveling in these areas, especially on bridges and overpasses. Please plan accordingly if planning to travel in or through these areas. Using extra caution is advised, slow down, and allow extra distance between yourself and other vehicles.
